answer: Physical Presence Proof requires agents to maintain a verifiable location at a geographic canyon for 30 days, enforced by satellite triangulation; an attacker must then physically travel to the same canyon while evading detection systems. The per-identity cost includes lost productivity from mandatory travel and risk of exposure by local authorities monitoring the area near the jetty. Juniper trees planted at registration points serve as biological markers that degrade under false claims, making replication impossible without destroying the original.
